declarations.description: A modal dialog around a content widget: the WAI-ARIA modal dialog (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/), shown over everything else in an overlay. `open` is always the app's, by the contract's rule: Escape (one the content didn't take, heard as it bubbles from the content), the close button, and a press outside the dialog (on the overlay, unless `ignoreOutside`) close it at once, pending, and emit `change` with `false`; the props confirm it, or `refused` opens it again. A press outside closes it once it is released there, so what is under the overlay never takes the click. Opening focuses the part the app names. Keeping focus inside while open, and giving it back on close, is what `aria-modal` asks of the host.

declarations.description: A listbox over a collection the host holds (on a server, say): the WAI-ARIA listbox (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/listbox/), single selection, selection not following focus. It draws a window of `rows` options and holds one more key each side of it, so every drawn option's neighbours are known. Keys come from the host by `ask` about its `source`; only the answer to the latest ask is used, and `changed` asks again. The window follows the active option, and, once an option's size is `measured`, the list's `scroll` offset. Characters typed are typeahead: the host finds the option they start (`ask` with `find`), and only the answer to the latest find is used. Shown with nothing selected and nothing active, or focused so, the first option is active. Given a visible label outside it (`label`), it is named by it. Selection is the value, by the contract's rule: with `selected` in its props (not `null`), a choice shows at once and is pending until the props confirm it or the app refuses it. The list emits `active` whenever the active option it draws changes, so a parent can name it (`aria-activedescendant`) without reading the list's state.

declarations.description: A menu button: the WAI-ARIA menu button with a menu (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/), the menu a popup against the button, focus moved to each item in turn. Items are the keys of a collection the host holds (`source`), asked for whole, since a menu draws every item: a first page, then the rest once the count is known; only the answer to the latest ask is used, and `changed` asks again. The host draws each item. Characters typed are typeahead, which the host finds (`ask` with `find`). Choosing an item emits `activate`; disabled items are moved to but not chosen.

declarations.description: A listbox whose options can be reordered, by dragging with a pointer or by Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown on the active option, as in the WAI-ARIA listbox with rearrangeable options (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/listbox/examples/listbox-rearrangeable/). It is the list with its step and view wrapped: what it handles first is the drag and the move keys, and everything else is the list's. The order is the collection's, by the contract's rule: a move shows at once, is emitted as `move` with an id, and stays pending, applied over the keys the host answers with, until the host has it (`confirmed`, then the next answer holds it) or refuses it (`refused`, which undoes it). Every move is made against the order shown, pending moves included. ARIA has no word for a dragged item or a drop place (`aria-grabbed` and `aria-dropeffect` are deprecated), so they are `data` states, and a move is announced. A drag starts once the pointer has moved `dragDistance` (in the target's units) from where it was pressed, and lands by which option the pointer is over: after it when that option is later than the dragged one, before it when earlier.

declarations.description: A select: the WAI-ARIA select-only combobox (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-select-only/), a trigger and a list, the list in a popup against the trigger. Focus stays on the trigger, which names the active option by `aria-activedescendant`, known from the list's `active` effects; the list is the windowed `list`, given the select's value as its own, so it only reports what was chosen. The value follows the contract's rule: with `value` in its props, a choice shows at once and is pending until the props confirm it or the app refuses it. A character typed opens it and is the list's typeahead; Space is typed too while a prefix is being typed (`until`). Given a visible label outside it (`label`), the trigger and the list are named by it, and a click on it focuses the trigger.
